definition: The probabilistic relevance model was devised by Stephen E.
details: Robertson and Karen Spärck Jones as a framework for probabilistic models to come. It is a formalism of information retrieval useful to derive ranking functions used by search engines and web search engines in order to rank matching documents according to their relevance to a given search query. It is a theoretical model estimating the probability that a document dj is relevant to a query q. The model assumes that this probability of relevance depends on the query and document representations. Furthermore, it assumes that there is a portion of all documents that is preferred by the user as the answer set for query q. Such an ideal answer set is called R and should maximize the overall probability of relevance to that user. The prediction is that documents in this set R are relevant to the query, while documents not present in the set are non-relevant. s i m ( d j , q ) = P ( R | d → j ) P ( R ¯ | d → j ) {\displaystyle sim(d_{j},q)={\frac {P(R|{\vec {d}}_{j})}{P({\bar {R}}|{\vec {d}}_{j})}}}

explainer.lead: The probabilistic relevance model is a formalism of information retrieval that estimates the probability a document is relevant to a query. It matters because it underpins ranking functions used by search engines.

tiers.eli5: It asks, for each document, how likely it is to be what you're looking for, and ranks them by that likelihood.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to derive ranking functions that order matching documents by estimated relevance to a query. A pitfall is that the estimate depends on how queries and documents are represented, so representation choices shape the ranking.
tiers.paperLevel: Devised by Stephen E. Robertson and Karen Spärck Jones as a framework for probabilistic models, it estimates the probability that a document dj is relevant to a query q, assuming this probability depends on the query and document representations; ranking functions are derived from it.

explainer.example: For a query q, the model estimates the relevance probability of each matching document dj and ranks them by that estimate.
